name: Sky
lede: Sky is a pale blue whose 'sky blue' phrasing Maerz and Paul trace to 1586, the earliest date, though the exact swatch itself turns up in only six of our archive's paintings.

sections.title: The oldest name in this batch
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul trace a 'sky blue' phrasing back to 1586, the earliest first-recorded date anywhere, and the Inter-Society Color Council's 1955 census files related Sky-family blues across two neighboring blocks, 181 and 185 [1]. This exact swatch, #82CAFC, is also independently listed by xkcd's 2010 crowd-sourced survey, the CSS color keywords, and Wikipedia, which is why ColorHub's library cites all four sources together [1].

Its closest library neighbor, within two units, is a near-duplicate name, *Light Sky Blue* [1]. Among colors with their own distinct name and page, the nearest are [[aero]], [[light-cornflower-blue]], and [[baby-blue-eyes]], each four to five units off, with [[sky-blue]] a little further at just over six [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this exact shade in only 6 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, reading as a highlight two-thirds of the time [2]. The small sample makes any painter or country pattern unreliable here [2]. Michel Pastoureau's history of blue argues that pale, sky-toned blues were long a minor color in Europe, overtaken in status by black, white, and red [3]. He dates its rise to a favorite only to the eighteenth century, a claim about the real sky's place in culture, not a measurement of this specific library swatch [3]. The archive count is a computed color match on varnished, photographed canvases, never a pigment identification [2].
